The buy block that used to sit here said Walmart does not carry capers in a normal jar size and kept piccata blocked for five days. It was simply false. The dish still works without it, just flatter, and the app tells you how to compensate. $2.27, and any grocery or corner store has it, so do not wait for another Walmart order

sweetpotato.label: Sweet potato, 1 kg
sweetpotato.note: Keep it out of the fridge, somewhere cool and dark. Cold turns its starch to sugar and gives it a hard core that never softens.

arugula.label: Arugula, about 120 g
arugula.note: The most perishable thing in the kitchen. Bagged greens turn to slime rather than going obviously off, so there is no warning.

beef.label: Browned beef, 3 bags (700 g)
beef.note: Cooked and bagged the evening of Aug 4: 250 g, 250 g and 200 g. Browned beef gets 3 to 4 days in the fridge against 1 to 2 raw. Anything you will not cook by Friday goes in the freezer, where it keeps 3 months.

lemon_fresh.note: Distinct from the bottle on purpose. In a sauce where lemon is one of three flavours, they are not the same ingredient. Bought 2026-08-09 as a 908 g bag.

parsley.note: Bought 2026-08-04 for Chicken Piccata and reported going mushy on 2026-08-08. Events for it were already in the database with no catalogue row here, which meant the validator could not resolve any recipe that reached for it. Added 2026-08-09.

turkeydeli.note: Deli slices, already cooked. High in sodium per the label, so anything built on it needs less added salt.

chickendeli.note: Fully cooked deli slices. Deliberately a separate id from `chickenbreast`, which is raw and frozen. A recipe that reaches for one must never resolve to the other.

pineapple.note: Frozen chunks. Raw pineapple carries bromelain, an enzyme that breaks protein down, so it curdles dairy if left to sit and it will not set in gelatin. Fine in a shake drunk straight away.

montereyjack.note: Semi-soft, melts smoothly, jalapeno already in it. Where mozzarella stretches, this one flows, so it suits a quesadilla or eggs rather than a pizza.

spaghetti_cooked.note: Distinct from the dry Barilla in the pantry on purpose: a recipe that wants cold cooked pasta must never resolve to a box of dry pasta, and one that wants dry must never resolve to this. Same reasoning as chickendeli versus chickenbreast. Plain, no sauce, confirmed by Silvio 2026-08-12. Cooked pasta gets 3 to 5 days.

His words: "Why is cooked spaghetti in the list? This is a shopping list. It doesn't make sense." chickenwings.note: Drumette and winglet, bone-in. Freeze-by on the label is Aug 21.

chickenthighs.note: Bone-in skin-on. At $7.63/kg this is the cheapest protein per dollar in the kitchen. Freeze-by Aug 21. Deliberately separate from chickenbreast and from the deli slices: a recipe wanting thighs must never resolve to breast, which cooks differently and dries out.

basil.note: 28 g packet. The most perishable thing in the kitchen, 2 to 3 days. Hates cold: stand the stems in water on the counter or keep it in the fridge DOOR, never the coldest shelf. Not interchangeable with dried basil or with Italian seasoning in anything where it goes in raw at the end.

blackvinegar.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18, not owned. Chinkiang, also spelled Zhenjiang, is a dark malty rice vinegar and it is NOT the distilled white vinegar in the cupboard: it is the sour note in General Tso and in most northern Chinese sauces. Gold Plum 554 ml was $2.99 at Superstore on 2026-08-18. Walmart lists Hengshun at $3.97 on an alphanumeric SKU, which is the marketplace pattern, so the shelf is unproven there.

driedchilli.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18, not owned. Distinct from the fresh chilli gap, from chili powder and from crushed red pepper: these are whole dried pods that go into hot oil for aroma. Omnivore Cookbook General Tso wants 7 to 8 and her footnote says they add aroma rather than heat. Tastie Dried Red Chili 120 g was $2.29 at Superstore on 2026-08-18, and it is not sold as Chinese or Korean, which is his call to make.

tomatoes_round.note: Round slicing tomatoes on the vine, 5 of them, receipt photo 20260814_121315 and the count stated by Silvio. Distinct from the grape tomatoes and from anything tinned. Catalogued 2026-08-18: it had existed only as stock_event 74, so validate.mjs refused a recipe pointing at it and the app printed the raw id where a name belongs.

beanmedley.note: UNCERTAIN COUNT, per stock_event 71: two receipt photos seven seconds apart may be one can twice or two cans, recorded as 1. Ask before a recipe leans on two. Catalogued 2026-08-18 for the same reason as tomatoes_round, and because burrito and chilli recipes are rejected for kidney beans while this sits in the pantry unmatched.

tomatoes_grape.note: 1.5 lb / 680 g, clearance. The first FRESH tomato in this kitchen. Distinct from tinned chopped tomatoes, from tomato sauce and from tomato paste, all of which behave differently in a sauce. Keep on the counter: the fridge kills the flavour and makes the texture mealy.

whiteonion.note: Two, bought 2026-08-12. NOT the same as the sweet onions under `yellowonion`, and the difference matters: white is sharper and cleaner, sweet holds more sugar and water and collapses faster. Recipes asking specifically for white onion can now be satisfied exactly instead of substituted.

sriracha.note: Listed under fridge condiments in KITCHEN.md. Had an alias set but NO catalogue row, so it could never be in stock and 190 recipe lines reported a shortage of something he owns.

Two different foods that a recipe treats completely differently, and printing them one above the other as "ground beef" twice is what read as a broken app on 2026-08-13. Events have existed for this id since 2026-08-11; the catalogue row was missing until 2026-08-14, which made every recipe pointing at it fail validation.

brownsugar.note: NOT the white sugar. Added to the catalogue 2026-08-14 because it is the single thing standing between this kitchen and a published Mongolian ground beef recipe it otherwise satisfies exactly (Salt & Lavender, 4.92 from 25 ratings). Her sauce is a third of a cup of it. White sugar, honey and maple syrup are all in the cupboard and any of them is a substitution, which only Silvio may decide.

vanilla.note: Compliments ARTIFICIAL Vanilla Extract, 250 mL, read off the label in photo 20260817_222001. Artificial means vanillin rather than bean extract: in the 31 corpus lines that bake it, that is a flavour difference and not a functional one. Bought 2026-08-17 at a Sobeys or Safeway, since Compliments is their brand.

chocolatechips.note: Compliments Dark Chocolate Chips, 225 g, read off the label in photo 20260817_222004. CHIPS, not a bar: chips carry stabilisers that hold their shape, so a recipe asking for chopped chocolate to melt smoothly is a substitution rather than a match. Bought 2026-08-17.

cilantro.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18, the evening a bunch arrived (photo 20260818_181607). Sold as cilantro here and as coriander in British recipes, and the SAME plant as Peruvian culantro in every recipe this kitchen will meet, though true culantro (Eryngium foetidum) is a different, stronger leaf. It is what makes Peruvian arroz con pollo green. Stems carry more flavour than leaves and Peruvian recipes blend both. Parsley looks identical and tastes nothing like it, so it is never a swap. Lasts about a week standing in water in the fridge, three days loose.

jalapeno.note: Your Fresh Market, 225 g bag, product of Mexico, bought 2026-08-18 (photo 20260818_181512). Rated MEDIUM on the pack. Distinct from the crushed jalapeno in the spice rack and from crushed red pepper: this is the fresh fruit, and the fresh fruity note is the thing the dried forms cannot give. Most of the heat is in the white pith, not the seeds, so deseeding-and-depithing is the volume control.

ajiamarillo.note: The backbone chilli of Peruvian cooking, from the yellow Peruvian chilli. Fruity and mildly hot rather than sharp, and it is a COLOUR as much as a flavour. Jalapeno is not a substitute in either direction: Peruvian recipes written for North American shops swap ají amarillo OUT for jalapeno because it is hard to find, never the reverse. Bought 2026-08-18. Quantity small, stated by Silvio as "not much but should be enough". Paste keeps months in the fridge once opened.

beer.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18 for Peruvian arroz con pollo, where beer is a real ingredient rather than a drink: cilantro is blended INTO it and the whole thing becomes the braising liquid. Classic Peruvian recipes name a dark malty beer (Cusquena Negra) and America’s Test Kitchen allows any smooth malty beer. The eatatourtable recipe this kitchen matched just says "1 12 oz beer" with no style, so whatever he bought satisfies her line exactly. STYLE NOT YET READ: a can is visible in the background of photo 20260818_181612 and its label was not legible.

asparagus.note: Ocean Mist Farms, 1 bunch, product of Mexico, bought 2026-08-18 (photo 20260818_181521). Nothing in the recipe catalogue asks for it yet, so it arrived unassigned. Highly perishable: 3 to 4 days, and it keeps best standing upright in a little water like cut flowers.

limes.note: Catalogued 2026-08-18. Events for it existed from 2026-08-08, when a 1.5 lb bag came home on clearance at $1.97, and there was never a row here to hang them on, so the id resolved to nothing. NOT the same as the bottled ReaLime, which is item `lemon`: bottled juice cannot be cut into a wedge and squeezed over a bowl, and every recipe that says "lime wedges" means the fruit.

jasminerice.note: Great Value Thai Jasmine Rice, 2 kg bag, bought 2026-08-18 (photo 20260818_215127). Catalogued as its own item on the same day, because `jasmine rice` had been an alias of `longgrainrice` and the two are not the same thing on the plate: jasmine is aromatic and cooks slightly softer and stickier, plain long grain stays neutral with the grains separate. Folding them together meant a recipe naming jasmine was answered from the long grain bag with nothing said about the difference. validate.mjs already knew they were different and carried separate RICE_RATIO entries for both.

broccoli.note: Added 2026-08-21. Stated by Silvio that day as bought on an untracked trip along with the 30 eggs and the asparagus. Given its own id rather than being left inside the `green vegetables` known-gap, which is the reason 78 dishes stayed blocked while he owned broccoli: a gap bucket is a CATEGORY, and a category cannot be partly satisfied. Buying one of the 32 vegetables inside it moved nothing.

bananas.note: Added 2026-08-22. He stated THREE RIPE BANANAS IN THE FREEZER at the start of the 08-21 session, said it again on 08-22, and it was never logged, so every banana recipe in the corpus read "no bananas" while they sat in his freezer. His words: "I told you in the first moment that I opened this session that I have three ripe bananas in the freezer. If I said so already, why isnt it anywhere in the app?" A fact he states out loud and an agent does not write down is worse than one nobody knew.

chickenthighs_boneless.note: Catalogued 2026-08-22, not owned. Split off `chickenthighs`, which is BONE-IN SKIN-ON and whose alias list was claiming boneless as well. ricevinegar.note: Catalogued 2026-08-22, not owned. Made by fermenting rice wine a second time into acid: about 4% and slightly sweet, against the 5% and flatly sour of the distilled white in the cupboard. NOT the Shaoxing wine or the mirin bought 2026-08-04, both of which are rice WINES and contain no vinegar at all. Stands behind 83 corpus dishes currently answered by substituting white.
